mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate used in equity valuation models, leading to higher present values of future cash flows and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, or Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals weakening labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power, leading to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or Rank IC over 3 years is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations fall, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction term regression coefficient is non-negative with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), supply chain disruptions intensify, causing higher input costs and reduced corporate margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to the tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, or Rank IC over 2 years is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market conditions, indicated by rising employment (PAYEMS > 155 million), boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 155 million, or Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and decline in housing starts (HOUST < 1300 thousand) indicates a dual stress on household purchasing power and the real estate sector, causing a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and HOUST < 1300, or interaction term regression coefficient is non-negative with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) reflects weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate investment and economic growth prospects, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
